title: Profit & Loss with Successive Discounts
questionText: A retailer in Hazratganj, Lucknow marks up the price of an article by 40% above its cost price. He then allows two successive discounts of 15% and 10% to a customer. If the cost price is ₹2,500, what is the net profit or loss incurred by the retailer?
explanation:
Cost Price (CP) = ₹2500.
Marked Price (MP) = 2500 × 1.40 = ₹3500.
Selling Price after 1st discount of 15% = 3500 × 0.85 = ₹2975.
Selling Price after 2nd discount of 10% = 2975 × 0.90 = ₹2677.50.
Net Profit = SP - CP = 2677.50 - 2500 = ₹177.50 profit.

title: Time, Speed & Relative Velocity
questionText: Two express trains start simultaneously from Lucknow Charbagh and Varanasi Cantt towards each other at speeds of 72 km/h and 54 km/h respectively. When they meet, the first train has traveled 54 km more than the second train. Find the total railway track distance between Lucknow and Varanasi.
explanation:
Let time until meeting be t hours.
Distance traveled by Train 1 = 72t.
Distance traveled by Train 2 = 54t.
Given: 72t - 54t = 54 km => 18t = 54 => t = 3 hours.
Total distance = 72(3) + 54(3) = 216 + 162 = 378 km.

title: Work Efficiency & Alternating Shifts
questionText: P, Q, and R can complete a software module in 12, 15, and 20 days respectively. P works on all days, while Q and R assist P on alternate days starting with Q on day 1. In how many days will the software module be completed?
explanation:
Total work = LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60 units.
Efficiency of P = 60/12 = 5 units/day.
Efficiency of Q = 60/15 = 4 units/day.
Efficiency of R = 60/20 = 3 units/day.
Day 1 (P + Q) = 5 + 4 = 9 units.
Day 2 (P + R) = 5 + 3 = 8 units.
In a 2-day cycle: 9 + 8 = 17 units.
In 3 cycles (6 days): 17 × 3 = 51 units.
Remaining work = 60 - 51 = 9 units.
Day 7: (P + Q) completes 9 units.
Total days = 6 + 1 = 7 days.

title: Combinatorics & Probability
questionText: A committee of 5 students is to be formed from 6 CSE students and 4 IT students of SMS Lucknow. What is the probability that the committee contains at least 3 CSE students?
explanation:
Total ways to choose 5 from 10: 10C5 = 252.
Favorable cases (at least 3 CSE):
1) 3 CSE & 2 IT: 6C3 × 4C2 = 20 × 6 = 120
2) 4 CSE & 1 IT: 6C4 × 4C1 = 15 × 4 = 60
3) 5 CSE & 0 IT: 6C5 × 4C0 = 6 × 1 = 6
Total favorable = 120 + 60 + 6 = 186.
Probability = 186 / 252 = 31 / 42.

questionText:

(A) Neither the head of the department / (B) nor the visiting professors from IIT / (C) were convinced by the proposed hypothesis / (D) because of its lack of empirical verification.
explanation: In "neither... nor..." constructions, the verb agrees with the closer subject ("visiting professors" is plural, so plural verb "were convinced" is grammatically correct). Hence there is no error.

title: Circular Seating Arrangement with Facing Directions
questionText: Eight engineers (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H) sit around a circular conference table facing the center. B sits third to the right of F. D is an immediate neighbor of neither B nor F. H sits second to the left of D. C sits between A and G. E sits to the immediate left of B. Who sits opposite to H?
explanation:
Placing positions 1 through 8 clockwise:
Let F be at 1. B is 3rd to right -> position 4.
E is immediate left of B -> position 3.
D cannot be neighbor of B (3, 5) or F (8, 2). Thus D must be at 6 or 7.
If D is at 6, H (2nd to left of D) is at 8. H is directly opposite E (position 4 steps away in 8-person circle: pos 4 vs pos 8 or pos 3 vs pos 7). In the resolved arrangement, opposite to H is E.

title: Coded Blood Relations
questionText:
Read the definitions:
"P + Q" means P is the father of Q.
"P - Q" means P is the sister of Q.
"P × Q" means P is the brother of Q.
"P ÷ Q" means P is the mother of Q.
Which of the following expressions indicates that "M is the maternal grandmother of T"?
explanation:
M maternal grandmother of T means M is mother of T's mother.
In M ÷ K ÷ T:
M ÷ K means M is mother of K.
K ÷ T means K is mother of T.
Therefore M is mother of K (who is mother of T) => M is maternal grandmother of T.

title: Syllogisms with "Only a few" Qualifiers
questionText:
Statements:
1. Only a few algorithms are neural networks.
2. All neural networks are models.
3. No model is a hardware circuit.

Conclusions:
I. Some algorithms are definitely not hardware circuits.
II. Some algorithms are not neural networks.

options.text: Both Conclusion I and II follow

explanation:
"Only a few algorithms are neural networks" strictly means both: "Some algorithms are neural networks" AND "Some algorithms are NOT neural networks" (so Conclusion II is definitely true).
Also, the algorithms that are neural networks are models, and no model is a hardware circuit; so those algorithms cannot be hardware circuits (Conclusion I is true). Hence both follow.

title: Data Sufficiency on Order & Ranking
questionText:
Among six candidates (P, Q, R, S, T, U) who secured ranks in SMS campus drive, who got the third rank?
Statement I: P scored higher than Q and R, but scored lower than T.
Statement II: S scored higher than T. U scored the least.

options.text: Neither nor both statements together are sufficient

explanation:
From I: T > P > (Q, R).
From II: S > T, and U is lowest.
Combining: S > T > P > {Q, R} > U.
Here the ranks are: 1st: S, 2nd: T, 3rd: P, 4th/5th: Q or R, 6th: U.
P is uniquely established as the 3rd rank holder. Thus both statements together are sufficient.

title: Advanced Modular Arithmetic & Remainder Theorem
questionText: Find the remainder when (37^105 + 23^105) is divided by 60.
explanation:
For any odd integer n, (a^n + b^n) is always divisible by (a + b).
Here n = 105 (odd), a = 37, b = 23.
a + b = 37 + 23 = 60.
Since (37^105 + 23^105) is an exact multiple of 60, the remainder upon division by 60 is 0.

title: Geometric Probability in Continuous Domain
questionText: Two random real numbers x and y are chosen uniformly and independently from the interval [0, 2]. What is the probability that their sum (x + y) is less than 2, given that (x^2 + y^2) is less than or equal to 4?
explanation:
Area of sample space: quadrant of circle of radius 2 in first quadrant = (1/4) × π × 2^2 = π.
Favorable area: triangle bounded by x >= 0, y >= 0, and x + y <= 2. Its vertices are (0,0), (2,0), (0,2).
Area of triangle = (1/2) × 2 × 2 = 2.
Probability = Favorable Area / Total Area = 2 / π.

title: Complex Logic Puzzle & Binary Truth-Tellers
questionText:
On an island, inhabitants are either Knights (always speak truth) or Knaves (always lie). Three inhabitants A, B, and C state:
A says: "All of us are Knaves."
B says: "Exactly one of us is a Knight."
What are the identities of A, B, and C?

options.text: A is Knave, B is Knight, C is Knave
A is Knight, B is Knave, C is Knight
A is Knave, B is Knave, C is Knight

explanation:
If A were Knight, then "all are knaves" would be true, which is contradictory. Thus A is a Knave.
Since A is a Knave, his statement is false (so not all are knaves; at least one knight exists).
Suppose B is a Knight: Then B speaks the truth, meaning "Exactly one of us is a Knight". Since B is that single Knight, A is Knave and C must be Knave. This is consistent! Identity: A is Knave, B is Knight, C is Knave.

# Reference Model Solution (Kadane's Algorithm - O(N) Time, O(1) Space)
import sys

def max_energy_sum(n, arr):
    max_so_far = arr[0]
    curr_max = arr[0]
    for i in range(1, n):
        curr_max = max(arr[i], curr_max + arr[i])
        max_so_far = max(max_so_far, curr_max)
